title: One Day in Busan: Temple, Haeundae Beach and Spa
intro: Follow Busan’s east coast for a day of sea views, temple steps, beach snacks and a Korean spa. This practical itinerary keeps the stops on one side of the city, with simple transport advice and options for a longer stay.

busan-east-coast-overview.note: East coast stops in visit order

busan-day-route.note: Follow the coast, then return to Haeundae

segments.voice: Busan stretches a long way along the coast, so trying to cross the whole city in one day can eat up your time. This plan stays on the east side, where the sea, the beach and your afternoon spa are all part of one easy route.

Begin at a Buddhist temple perched above the water. Then head back toward Haeundae for a beach walk, a casual lunch and, later, a slow afternoon in a Korean spa. It is a full day, but the stops make sense together.
The day ends back by the sea. Have dinner near Haeundae Beach, then enjoy the shoreline after dark or take a short taxi ride to Gwangalli Beach for a view of the lit-up Gwangan Bridge.

Here is the route at a glance: start at Haedong Yonggungsa, return to Haeundae for the beach and market, continue to Centum City for the spa, then come back for dinner. The order keeps your day focused on one side of Busan.
Let’s make one day in Busan feel straightforward, with a clear route, realistic travel advice and a few good choices if you have extra time.

card.title: One Day on the East Coast

segments.voice: A little planning makes this route much easier. The biggest decision is whether you are sleeping in Busan or arriving from Seoul, because the temple and Haeundae are not near Busan Station.

card.title: A Few Useful Checks
card.sub: Plan the day before you set out

segments.voice: Coming from Seoul, the KTX from Seoul Station to Busan Station takes about two and a half hours. From Busan Station, allow about an hour by subway, changing from Line One to Line Two, or stay near Haeundae the night before.

For this plan, staying near Haeundae is a practical choice, especially if you want to start early at the temple. If you are taking the KTX down and back in one day, know that it is possible, but it makes for a long day.
The transit card you use in Seoul also works on Busan subways and buses. Bring the same card if you have one, and check current routes in Naver Map or KakaoMap before you leave for each stop.

Check opening hours on a map app on the day, especially for SPA LAND and the Blueline Park. In summer and on weekends, sky capsule tickets can sell out, so book ahead if that ride is part of your plan.

chapters.name: One Day on the East Coast

segments.voice: This is the route for your day: temple first, then Haeundae Beach and its nearby market, followed by SPA LAND in Centum City. Finish back near the beach for dinner. Start early, and use a taxi for the temple if you want the simplest trip.
The route map keeps the day in visit order. The morning trip north to the temple is the longest move; after that, the beach, market, spa and dinner fit into a more compact east-side plan.

Start at Haedong Yonggungsa in Gijang, a Buddhist temple built on rocks above the sea. It is one of the few Korean temples on the shoreline instead of in the mountains. Go early, because it gets busy from mid-morning.
Allow about an hour at the temple. There are steps down to the main hall, so take your time. This is a place of worship: keep your voice low, and be considerate when taking photos.

A taxi from Haeundae to the temple takes around twenty to thirty minutes, depending on traffic. Local buses also run. Check the current route in Naver Map or KakaoMap, and show the driver the name on your map app if you need to.

Head back to Haeundae Beach for a walk on the sand and the promenade. Summer weekends can be very busy, so an early start helps. Keep the beach for late morning, after your quieter visit to the temple.
For an easy lunch stop, walk into the streets behind the beach and visit Haeundae Traditional Market. It is close to the sand and is a handy place to pick up snacks such as fish cakes and tteokbokki.

If you have time, the Haeundae Blueline Park runs a beach train and small sky capsules along the old coastal railway, between Mipo near the end of the beach and Cheongsapo. Tickets can sell out at busy times, so book ahead in summer and on weekends.

In the afternoon, take Line Two one stop from Haeundae to Centum City. SPA LAND is inside Shinsegae Centum City department store, with hot-spring baths and themed rest rooms. It is a comfortable introduction to Korean bathhouse culture.

The spa and department store are in the same building, so you can also shop there or spend longer indoors if the weather is poor. Check the spa’s opening hours before you go, and look up basic bathhouse rules if this is your first Korean spa.

Return to Haeundae for dinner. Ribs of Legend Haeundae is close to the beach and serves Korean grilled ribs. Afterward, walk along the shoreline at night, or take a short taxi ride to Gwangalli Beach.

At Gwangalli, the Gwangan Bridge is lit up after dark. If you have more time and a car or taxi budget, Waveon Coffee is a well-known sea-view cafe on the Gijang coast, north of Haeundae. The west side of Busan is better saved for another day.

You do not need to plan a complicated cross-city route for this day. The main transfer is from Haeundae to Centum City on Line Two, just one stop. The longer trip is the temple visit, north-east of Haeundae.

For Haedong Yonggungsa, a taxi is the simplest option from Haeundae and takes around twenty to thirty minutes depending on traffic. Local buses also run, but check the current route before setting out.

Use Naver Map or KakaoMap for current bus and subway directions. They are useful for checking the route on the day, but opening hours should also be checked before you go, especially for the spa and the Blueline Park.

The Seoul transit card you already use works on Busan’s subways and buses. Keep it handy for the ride between Haeundae and Centum City, and avoid adding extra city crossings that do not fit this east-coast day.
A few small choices can make this day feel rushed. Keep these common planning mistakes in mind before you leave your hotel or book an extra activity.

card.title: Four Easy Mistakes
card.sub: A smoother Busan day starts here

segments.voice: Watch out for these four things: starting late at the temple, treating a Seoul day trip as an easy outing, forgetting to check current hours, and leaving popular sky capsule tickets until the last minute.

list.heading: Avoid These
items: Waiting too long to book sky capsules

segments.voice: Starting early matters because the temple gets busy from mid-morning. A day trip from Seoul is possible by KTX, but it makes for a long day. Check hours on the day, and book sky capsules ahead in summer and on weekends if you want to ride.

Here are quick answers to four useful questions: can you come from Seoul for the day, what is the easiest way to reach the temple, does the plan work in rain, and where should you stay for this route?

Can you visit from Seoul in one day? Yes. The KTX makes it possible, but the return journey and this full itinerary make for a long day. You will see more if you stay at least one night, ideally near Haeundae.

What is the easiest way to reach Haedong Yonggungsa? Take a taxi from Haeundae. It takes around twenty to thirty minutes depending on traffic. Local buses also go there, and Naver Map or KakaoMap can show the current route.

label.title: How Do I Reach the Temple?

segments.voice: Does this plan work on a rainy day? Partly. The temple and beach are outdoors, but SPA LAND and Shinsegae Centum City are indoors. If the weather is poor, you can stretch the afternoon there.

Where should you stay? For this itinerary, stay near Haeundae if you can. It makes an early temple start easier and keeps you close to the beach, market and evening dinner after your visit to Centum City.
The simple version is this: start early at Haedong Yonggungsa, spend late morning around Haeundae Beach and its market, take a slow afternoon at SPA LAND, then return to the sea for dinner.

Keep the route on Busan’s east side. Use a taxi or check local buses for the temple, use your transit card on the subway, and check opening hours and sky capsule tickets before you go. Stay near Haeundae if you want an easier start.
